This is a large PR (104 files changed, +10187/-745, 65 commits) rebuilding the global header: logo, nav bar, mega menu, mobile drawer, Contentful-backed nav data. Two ready-to-use worktrees exist, both with node_modules already symlinked in and already gate-checked — do NOT re-run tsc/lint/test/audit:tokens, see my measured numbers below. Spend your budget on what those gates cannot see. - HEAD (the PR): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/113175e9-2496-4539-9640-84df14f78583/scratchpad/pr65/head - BASE (develop before this PR): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/113175e9-2496-4539-9640-84df14f78583/scratchpad/pr65/base Get the full diff yourself, e.g. from the main repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (both commits exist there too): `git diff 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99 10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d -- overrides/ scripts/contentful/ translations/` Rubric — read these yourself in the repo root: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (styling hierarchy, SFCC bridge pattern for internally-shared base components, co-located `.css.ts` recipes), `.claude/rules/components.md` (component/hook structure, Storybook categorisation), `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `.claude/rules/typescript.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` + `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` (this PR touches Tier 2 `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` — all Squad-A/Squad-B shared shell per `.claude/rules/squadA.md`), `.claude/rules/testing.md`, and `AGENTS.md`. Exemplar precedent: the footer decomposition (SFCC-55, already merged) is the established pattern this PR explicitly says it followed ("generalised footer's footerNavGroup into a shared navGroup type") — compare `overrides/app/components/footer/` structure/conventions against the new `overrides/app/components/header/` for consistency. Ticket requirements (already-gathered ground truth from Jira — do not re-fetch): SFCC-52 "Global Header UI" ACs (Desktop/Mobile unless marked): 1. Global header displayed at top of page, desktop and mobile. 2. Sticky on scroll. 3. Logo click navigates home. 4. Bag icon shows correct running item count. 5. Bag icon count updates live, no full reload. 6. (Desktop) All header icons (Search, Account, Saved, Bag) visible per Figma. 7. (Mobile) Hamburger top-left, Search + Bag top-right. 8. (Mobile) Tapping hamburger opens full-screen drawer, hamburger becomes close (×). 9. (Mobile) Tapping close (×) closes drawer, restores hamburger. 10. (Mobile) Drawer shows all top-level nav categories vertically, correct order per Figma. 11. (Mobile) Saved and Account links shown below main nav categories in the drawer. Note: SFCC-52's own reporter/PR-author (Tim Lavelle) commented on the ticket suggesting AC4/5 belong to a separate Cart story and AC8-11 belong to a Navigation story — but the Jira AC field itself was never edited to remove them, so they remain formally live ACs of this ticket. The ticket's own description also states: "Icon destinations (Search, Account, Wish List, Cart) are wired up as the underlying pages and features are built in their respective stories. The exception is the logo." SFCC-746 "Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful": supersedes the nav portion of SFCC-52. Nav items/order/storefront-visibility managed in Contentful, keyed by SFCC category taxonomy ID. Mega menu (desktop) and mobile hamburger/drill-down are explicitly OUT of scope here (covered by SFCC-96). Hover/focus/active visual states explicitly out of scope (defined in UI kit, not re-specified in this ticket). Author's own last comment: "most of this done except scroll behaviour and mega-menu... still need to test keyboard nav and accessibility... wired into Contentful but engineered to flip to SFCC." SFCC-747 "Logo Masthead": supersedes the logo portion of SFCC-52. Key ACs: desktop/tablet/mobile — logo left-aligned, own row below top nav. Link behaviour: click navigates home; if already on homepage, reload or no-navigation is acceptable (must not navigate away unexpectedly). Accessibility: AC8 — accessible name "Zimmermann" via `alt` on an `` OR `aria-label`+`role="img"` on an inline SVG. AC9 — link itself announced as "Zimmermann, go to homepage". **AC10 — the logo link must be the FIRST focusable element in the entire header, before any nav items or icons.** AC11 — visible focus ring meeting 3:1 contrast. Scroll behaviour explicitly out of scope (SFCC-93, separate ticket). Logo does not vary by storefront (static asset, not Contentful-managed). SFCC-96 "Expanded Navigation": desktop mega menu — hover/click a top-level nav item opens a full-width panel: left column (subcategory links then editorial links), right area (large campaign image), CLOSE control top-right. All content Contentful-managed, can vary per storefront. SFCC-97 "Expanded Navigation (Mobile)": hamburger opens full nav panel; drill-down pattern (tap heading → reveals subcategories, back control to return); Z.Immerse is a direct link (no drill-down); "Back in Boutique" category included; tapping a destination closes panel and navigates. **This ticket was archived 2026-08-24 ("all breakpoints covered in SFCC-96") — treat SFCC-96 as the current owner of this behaviour, not a separate open requirement.** My measured gate numbers, head vs base — already verified, do not redo: - `tsc --noEmit`: clean on both sides (exit 0). - `lint`: base 20 problems (4 errors/16 warnings, ALL pre-existing/inherited from develop — routes.tsx, recipeGuards.test.ts, the OLD header/index.tsx being replaced, product-view/index.tsx, product-detail/index.tsx — none of these are this PR's concern). Head: 24 problems (5 errors/19 warnings). Net-NEW introduced by this PR: 1 prettier error in new `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.test.ts:106`; warnings — 2 forbidden-non-null-assertion in new `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.stories.tsx:23-24`, 1 unused `_onLogoClick` var in `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx:135`, 2 unused props (`storeLocatorEnabled`, `onStoreLocatorClick`) in `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx:113,119` (worth checking whether a Store Locator icon is even in scope anywhere — it's not mentioned in any of the 5 tickets' ACs above), 1 non-null-assertion in new `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts:64`. - `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: base 4 unacknowledged violations (ALL pre-existing, in the OLD header being replaced by this PR). Head: 1 unacknowledged violation — NEW: `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:20` — `const BP_CONTENT_WRAP = '59.125em'; // 946px` — a bare px-conversion comment, which does NOT contain provisional/pending/placeholder/audit-allow, so per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` it does not qualify as an acknowledged exception. - `npm run test` (vitest): base 26 files/408 tests all passing; head 41 files/612 tests all passing. All green both sides — no regressions, substantial new coverage added. Already known — factor in, don't rediscover: (a) GitHub reports `mergeable: CONFLICTING` against current develop tip, but I traced it: the ONLY conflicting paths are `.claude/registry/components.md` and `.claude/registry/hooks.md`, both auto-generated by `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — not a real code conflict, just needs a merge + regenerate. (b) CodeRabbit posted a late chat-style "Approved ✅" reply in the PR thread, but this is NOT a real GitHub approval — `reviewDecision` is still `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, and that reply's own self-check only covers unresolved-and-non-outdated CodeRabbit review threads (0 found) — a weak check that also predates the PR's actual current head commit by one. Don't treat it as a clean bill of health; form your own view. Cover these angles (dispatch your own sub-agents per angle if that's how you work): 1. **Correctness and regression** — does the new header/nav/mega-menu/drawer logic actually do what it claims; behavioural bugs, race conditions, edge cases (empty/missing nav data from Contentful, fetch failure, locale mismatches, rapid open/close). 2. **Conventions, structure, and tier ownership** — does the new code match the rubric; anything mis-tiered, wrongly placed, or violating the Squad A/B coordination note in squadA.md (header/footer/drawer-menu/list-menu are Tier 2 shared-shell, "coordinate before touching"). 3. **Contract fidelity** — `list-menu` and `drawer-menu` are SFCC base-template paths other base components may import internally (check with `grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/list-menu'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` and the same for `drawer-menu`) — does the override keep its default export API-compatible per the "SFCC bridge pattern" in overrideStyling.md? Also check the new ui-kits atoms (`zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`) and the new `megaMenuContent` for internal consistency with sibling atoms (`zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`) already in the codebase. 4. **Failure modes and security** — Contentful fetch failure handling for nav data (`useHeaderNav.ts`) — does a failed/slow fetch break the header, per AGENTS.md's Graceful Degradation section ("each external system must fail independently")? Any XSS surface in Contentful-sourced nav labels/links/promo images (check for unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`)? 5. **Token and styling strategy** — beyond the one audit:tokens hit already found, look for bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, and state exhaustiveness (hover/focus/active/disabled all present per component, not just default) across the new `header.css.ts`, `leftBar.css.ts`, `rightBar.css.ts`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, `zimmSearchInput.css.ts`, `megaMenuContent.css.ts`, `listMenu.css.ts` recipes. For every finding: cite file:line, state what's wrong and why per which specific rule or AC, and note your own confidence. Everything you report will be independently re-verified before it's used, so err toward reporting anything plausible rather than self-censoring — but don't pad the list with nitpicks that bring no real value. Do not write or edit any code. Report findings only — I need a findings report back, not a fix.

1	/**
2	 * Shared menu-expansion state contract for the header's LeftBar/RightBar sections.
3	 *
4	 * Confirmed via Figma review (SFCC-52 follow-up): desktop/tablet, mobile-L1 (root drawer)
5	 * and mobile-L2 (drilled into a category) each have a *different* close-state treatment —
6	 * there is no single uniform "close button" shared across breakpoints. Modelled as a flat,
7	 * behaviour-named discriminated union (per typescript.md's "discriminated unions for
8	 * variant/state modeling") rather than nested per-breakpoint booleans, since the four states
9	 * are mutually exclusive and each maps to exactly one rendering contract in LeftBar/RightBar.
10	 *
11	 * Naming is behaviour-first, not breakpoint-first: desktop and tablet share the identical
12	 * `fullSwap` treatment (see RightBar), so there is no separate `expandedDesktop`/
13	 * `expandedTablet` pair, and the two mobile drawer depths get their own state each because
14	 * their rendering contracts genuinely differ (`mobileL1` is a same-control icon toggle,
15	 * `mobileL2` adds a back control on the left and a close control on the right).
16	 *
17	 * **Scope note for SFCC-96/97 (real wiring):** this branch (infra only) does not manage or
18	 * derive this value from any real mega-menu/drawer open state — `LeftBar`/`RightBar` both
19	 * default their `menuExpanded` prop to `'closed'` and the header shell
20	 * (`header/index.tsx`) does not pass one at all. Wiring a real value in here — driven by
21	 * the actual mega-menu/drawer open/close/drill-in state — is that follow-up work's job.
22	 */
23	export type MenuExpandedState =
24	  | 'closed'
25	  // Desktop/tablet: a mega menu or drawer is open. RightBar's entire icon cluster (search,
26	  // profile, wishlist, bag) is replaced by a single "Close" text + X control.
27	  | 'fullSwap'
28	  // Mobile: the root drawer (L1) is open. LeftBar's hamburger toggles to an X in place —
29	  // nothing else changes; RightBar is unaffected (search + bag stay as in 'closed').
30	  | 'mobileL1'
31	  // Mobile: drilled into a category from the root drawer (L2). LeftBar shows a back
32	  // chevron (returns to L1, does not close the drawer). RightBar keeps search + bag
33	  // visible and adds a close X alongside them — no account/wishlist icons at this depth.
34	  | 'mobileL2';

2	import type { HeaderNavItemEntry } from 'app/types/contentful';

4	export type DrawerMenuStateContextValue = {
5	  /** The L1 item currently drilled into, or `null` at L1. Only meaningful while `isDrilledIn`
6	   * is true — DrawerMenu reads this to know which item's columns to render as its L2 panel. */
7	  activeItem: HeaderNavItemEntry | null;
8	  /** Whether the drawer is showing the L2 (drilled-in) panel rather than the L1 root list. */
9	  isDrilledIn: boolean;
10	  /** Called by DrawerMenu when the shopper taps an L1 row that has columns (drills to L2). */
11	  drillInto: (item: HeaderNavItemEntry) => void;
12	  /** Called by DrawerMenu whenever its own `isOpen` prop (owned by base `_app`'s
13	   * `useDisclosure`, not by this hook — see useHeaderMenuExpandedState's own comment)
14	   * transitions to false. Keeps the header shell's chrome state in sync no matter how the
15	   * physical drawer actually closed (LeftBar/RightBar's own close controls, Escape, or an
16	   * overlay click all eventually flow through here). */
17	  notifyClosed: () => void;
18	  /** DrawerMenu registers its real `onClose` prop (the one it receives directly from base
19	   * `_app`) here on mount, so the header shell's LeftBar 'X' / RightBar close-icon — which
20	   * have no `onClose` prop of their own — can trigger the actual Chakra `<Drawer>` close.
21	   * Pass `null` to unregister on unmount. */
22	  registerCloseHandler: (fn: (() => void) | null) => void;
23	};
24	
25	const noop = () => undefined;
26	
27	/**
28	 * Static default so DrawerMenu (and its presentational view) can still render standalone in
29	 * Storybook/Vitest without a header-mounted Provider — same graceful-degradation shape as
30	 * useUiCopy (see .claude/rules/components.md's Context-backed-hook exception). A story/test
31	 * that needs to exercise real drill-in/close-registration behaviour should wrap with
32	 * `DrawerMenuStateContext.Provider` instead of relying on this default.
33	 */
34	export const DEFAULT_DRAWER_MENU_STATE: DrawerMenuStateContextValue = {
35	  activeItem: null,
36	  isDrilledIn: false,
37	  drillInto: noop,
38	  notifyClosed: noop,
39	  registerCloseHandler: noop,
40	};

42	/**
43	 * Shares mobile drawer L1↔L2 drill state between the header shell (`header/index.tsx`, via
44	 * `useHeaderMenuExpandedState`) and `DrawerMenu`, which base `_app.jsx` renders as one of
45	 * Header's `children` (redirected to our override through the `ccExtensibility` resolver) —

47	 * prop, since Header cannot see through whatever wrapper elements (`HideOnDesktop`, etc.)
48	 * base `_app.jsx` nests `<DrawerMenu>` inside.
49	 */

52	/**
53	 * Consumed by `DrawerMenu` to read/report L1↔L2 drill state that's actually owned by the
54	 * header shell. Degrades to `DEFAULT_DRAWER_MENU_STATE` with no Provider mounted, matching
55	 * useUiCopy's pattern — see that hook's own JSDoc for the reasoning.
56	 *
57	 * @returns the current drawer menu state/actions — see DrawerMenuStateContextValue.
58	 */
59	export const useDrawerMenuState = (): DrawerMenuStateContextValue =>

1	/**
2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
3	 *
4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
10	 *
11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
13	 */
14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
22	
23	/**
24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
25	 *
26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
30	 *
31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
33	 */
34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
35	
36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
37	
38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);
